text_blocks.snippet: A blocked left circumflex artery, also known as the LCx, can cause symptoms similar to other coronary artery disease issues, including chest pain (angina), shortness of breath, and fatigue. These symptoms may be accompanied by cold sweats, dizziness, heart palpitations, nausea, or pain in the shoulder, arm, neck, or jaw. Importantly, a blockage in the LCx can sometimes be difficult to diagnose with a standard ECG (electrocardiogram).
